articles.title: A Giant Heat Dome Is Baking the World Cup — Here's How Players and Fans Are Staying Safe
articles.summary: A massive heat dome is pushing temperatures above 110°F at World Cup games. In Kansas City, it could feel like 110°F for Colombia vs. Ghana. FIFA added water breaks, but some stadiums have no roof to block the sun.

articles.title: It's Not Just the Daytime Heat — Scorching Nights Are Making the Heat Wave Even More Dangerous
articles.summary: A heat dome is baking 90 million Americans, but nights aren't cooling down. In D.C. and Philly, temps stay above 80°F. Without AC, bodies can't recover, raising the risk of heat stroke. Climate change is making hot nights more common.

articles.title: England Almost Lost to a Tiny Nation — Until Harry Kane Saved the Day
articles.summary: England was 15 minutes from a shocking World Cup exit against DR Congo. Harry Kane scored twice to win 2-1. Coach Tuchel faces big problems: a shaky defense and too much reliance on Kane and Bellingham. Next up: Mexico in Mexico City.
